fix(managed): report metadata range failures at artifact file offsets (#3508)

ManagedMetadataLayout's range check reported offsets relative to the buffer
it was given: the metadata root for version and stream headers, and the
table stream for the tables header, row counts and table data. Other
diagnostics in the same reader already use artifact file offsets, so a
truncated table stream at file offset 888 was reported at offset 24, inside
the DOS header.

invalid-metadata-root issue carries a file offset.

fix(native): inspect arm64e.x1 slices by their exact name (#3500)

inspect_macho passed the CPU-family spelling (`arm64e`) for every dotted lipo
slice name to otool, nm, dwarfdump and vtool. That is right for the
pointer-auth ABI version suffix (`arm64e.v1`), but `arm64e.x1` is a distinct
subtype: on a universal x86_64 + arm64e.x1 executable otool failed with
"does not contain architecture: arm64e" and the whole inspection failed.

Strip only the `.v<N>` ABI version suffix and pass other variant names
exactly. vtool has no spelling for a variant subtype, so skip it for such
slices and report that build metadata comes from otool only.

fix(reconstruction): merge repeated observations into one generated obligation (#3524)

Two capture-process records of the same executable and scenario generate
the same obligation ID. addCandidate added their definition counts, so the
ledger reported duplicate-definition, a closure blocker meant for competing
definitions, merely because the claim was observed twice. The merge also
kept only the first record's unavailable_authority and
required_next_evidence.

Generated IDs digest their derivation key, so merging two generated
candidates keeps one definition. A reviewed definition that reuses an ID is
still a duplicate. The merge now unions unavailable_authority and
required_next_evidence from every observation.

fix(managed): charge admitted member facts once in the final projection (#3487)

* fix(managed): charge admitted member facts once in the final projection

inspect_managed_members admits method bodies, signatures, call edges,
field accesses and user strings as they are produced, then admits the
whole result again before returning it. The final pass re-counted every
already-admitted record, so the 64 MiB representation budget was spent
at roughly twice the result's JSON size. Ordinary assemblies such as
MathNet.Numerics, MongoDB.Driver, Npgsql, ClosedXML, System.Reactive and
Azure.Storage.Blobs returned resource-limit with no members.

The budget now remembers each admitted projection. A containing
projection spends that charge once instead of counting the subtree
again; a value that serializes more than once still pays for every
further occurrence. Results that already fit are byte-identical.

fix(cli): stop quietly when the stdout reader closes early (#3781)

* fix(cli): stop quietly when the stdout reader closes early

`rea ... | head` crashed once head closed the pipe. TOON and YAML output

in one entry-point function shared by both CLI branches; MCP stdio keeps

commits.subject: fix(javascript): keep empty URL path segments significant (#3792)
commits.body:
fix(javascript): keep empty URL path segments significant (#3792)

* fix(javascript): keep empty URL path segments significant

ESM imports and HTML script references were joined with POSIX path
rules, which collapse '//' before applying '..'. URL resolution removes
the empty segment instead, so './assets//../app.js' names assets/app.js,
not app.js, and the graph linked the importer and renderer to the wrong
file. URL references refused every '//' even when dot segments cancel it.

Resolve ESM, HTML (including document base) and URL references through
one URL dot-segment helper. A remaining empty segment stays unavailable,
references above the artifact root are still rejected, and CommonJS keeps
filesystem path semantics.

Fixes #3307

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(javascript): resolve HTML base and reference as one URL path

The base href was turned into a canonical path before the script
reference was applied. A base empty segment that the reference's '..'
would remove was rejected early, and an above-root '..' from the base
became a removable segment that the reference's '..' could cancel.

Keep one URL path state through base and reference resolution, with
above-root escapes held apart from removable segments, and reject empty
segments only in the final path. Remove the superseded htmlBaseDirectory.

fix(apple): report plist dates the decoder cannot represent as unknown (#3793)

plutil writes years past 9999 and negative years in a form the pinned
XML decoder cannot parse, and binary plists can hold dates outside the
JavaScript Date range. The decoder returns an Invalid Date. Its
projection's toISOString() call then threw, so inspect_plist failed the
whole plist as "unreadable_output" with a `rea doctor` remediation.

archive in the same way.

projectPlistValue, the shared projection, now reports such a date as
{ "$plist_type": "date", "iso8601": null } and counts it. inspect_plist,
keyed archive inspection and Interface Builder decoding each add a
counted limitation, as they already do for non-finite reals.

* fix(reference): stop attributing overwritten require members to Node

import-reference-source treated require.resolve(...) and require.main(...)
as Node's resolver even after the file replaced that member, so a literal
argument became a parsed internal dependency that the source never loads.

keep Node's identity: no write to either member or a computed member
(assignment, update, delete, destructuring) and no use of require as a
value where a mutator or alias could replace them. Bare require(...) calls
are unaffected.

accept optional calls before deciding the loader escaped, and add
controls for bare calls after a member overwrite, a local loader's
member write, and optional calls.

with O_NONBLOCK and verifies a regular file before any read. A FIFO,
directory or socket now fails admission immediately with the existing
regular-file error; symlink rejection and cancellation are unchanged.

`--filter-output=...`, `--token-limit=...` and `--token-offset=...`

commits.subject: fix(apktool): own the version probe's process group and keep its timeout typed (#3808)
commits.body:
fix(apktool): own the version probe's process group and keep its timeout typed (#3808)

* fix(apktool): own the version probe's process group and keep its timeout typed

The version probe ran its launcher through execFileOutput, which waits
for every inherited output pipe to close. A shell launcher's child that
holds those pipes outlived the stop request, so the probe stayed pending
past its deadline and its grace period, and cancellation hung the same
way. An expired probe also surfaced as a non-retryable unusable-version
refusal.

Run the probe through runOwnedCommand like the decode run, so the owned
process group is stopped with its children. Report its deadline as
AnalysisTimeoutError with timeout_ms and retain an unresolved cleanup
owner for close. Apktool launchers are interpreter scripts, so both the
probe and the decode run prove ownership by run token instead of the
launcher's argv prefix. A close with unresolved process cleanup reports
a typed ProviderCleanupError instead of an untyped AggregateError.

Fixes #3342
Fixes #3347
Fixes #3337

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(apktool): carry unresolved probe cleanup through both provider entry points

A probe failure other than cancellation or timeout, such as an output
overflow whose launcher child survives, now keeps its cleanup reason and
resources on ApktoolConfigurationFailure. inspectAvailability and execute
report it as ProviderCleanupError instead of ordinary unavailability or
capability_unavailable.

Add a real-process lifecycle test: an interpreter launcher starts a child
that holds the inherited output pipes, the probe is cancelled after
launch, and both processes must be stopped within the bound.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(apktool): ignore zombies and always clean up the probe lifecycle fixture

Treat a zombie as exited when checking the launcher and child, bound the
cancellation wait so a regressed probe still reaches cleanup, and stop
any remaining fixture processes in a finally block.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(apktool): treat a failed process inspection as unknown, not stopped

Only ESRCH, a zombie state or ps reporting no match counts as exited; a
ps launch failure leaves the process presumed live so the assertion
fails and the finally block still stops it.

perf(javascript): index object literal members for exact-key reference lookup (#3836)

semanticObjectPropertyReferences scanned every property of an object

fix(kuna): answer a repeated single-function request without re-running Kuna (#4169)

* fix(kuna): answer a repeated single-function request without re-running Kuna

A session dropped each single-function run once it settled, so a repeat
request for the same procedure re-ran `kuna decompile --addr`, which
analyzes the whole image again. After a failed export every pseudocode
request uses that path for the rest of the session.

Keep each completed text by entry address, within a 16 MiB least recently
used budget, until the export's reader is adopted or the session closes.
Failed and cancelled runs are not kept. The export's text still supersedes
a kept one.

commits.subject: fix(kuna): stream string scans instead of capping them at 16 MiB (#4318)
commits.body:
fix(kuna): stream string scans instead of capping them at 16 MiB (#4318)

* fix(kuna): stream string scans instead of capping them at 16 MiB

`list_strings` and `search_strings` buffered Kuna's whole string JSON and
refused anything above 16 MiB. Kuna writes about 290 bytes per row, so
every app above roughly 10 MB failed with a non-retryable memory error:
a 20 MB Ghostty binary produces 31 MB, Raycast 30 MB and an arm64
Firefox XUL 179 MB.

Parse the scan as Kuna writes it. `runOwnedCommand` accepts a stdout
sink, and `KunaStringInventoryReader` owns the interpretation: it
tokenizes synchronously with stream-json, keeps exact u64 address
tokens, validates each row before retaining it, skips members it does
not interpret, and admits retained rows against live heap headroom
rather than a fixed scan size. The first contradiction stops Kuna
instead of waiting for the rest; an incomplete document is judged only
after Kuna's own exit status. Diagnostics keep the 8 MiB Kuna budget,
now shared with the project export.

Refs #1957

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(kuna): admit string scan text as it streams and drop sinks with their command

Review found that packed string tokens were assembled whole before the
reader could discard them or check heap headroom, and that a stdout sink
could outlive a cancelled or timed-out command.

Move the token mechanics into `KunaJsonDocumentReader`: keys and numbers
(Kuna's own fields) stay packed, while strings, which carry target-derived
text, arrive in chunks. Ignored strings are dropped unassembled and kept
ones are admitted against live heap headroom as they grow. Kept text is
copied out of the decoded chunk it was sliced from, so retained rows no
longer pin whole chunks (XUL: 278 MB retained before, 156 MB after).
`KunaStringInventoryReader` keeps only the string-scan semantics.

`runOwnedCommand` now ties the stdout pipeline to the command's deadline
signal and aborts it when collection fails, destroying the sink.

Refs #1957

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(kuna): type the stream-json tokenizer where it is imported

The Reverse tools quality lane type-checks a partial project that reaches
KunaJsonStream without the separate streamJsonParser.d.ts augmentation,
so jsonParser had no declaration there. Declare the tokenizer's shape at
its only import site and remove the augmentation file, so every
compilation of the reader is self-contained. Split two helpers out of
the token dispatcher and simplify the stdout sink wait in
runOwnedCommand, which keeps the added complexity minimal.

Refs #1957

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(kuna): bound key and number assembly in streamed Kuna JSON

Review found that packed keys (and packed numbers) were assembled whole
by the tokenizer before the reader could discard or constrain them, so a
malformed scan with one enormous key could still exhaust the heap.

Stream every scalar. Keys are assembled only up to 64 code units, past
every field name the reader keeps, so a longer key is skipped unmatched;
kept numbers longer than that are rejected, and ignored numbers are
dropped unassembled. XUL's 611k-row scan parses in the same time.

Refs #1957

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(kuna): stream the call graph instead of capping it at 32 MiB (#4329)

* fix(kuna): stream the call graph instead of capping it at 32 MiB

Call relationships buffered `kuna decompile-graph` and refused output
above 32 MiB. A 53 MB Raycast binary produces a 157 MB graph (180k
functions, 773k edges), so every call query failed with a non-retryable
memory error after Kuna's minute-long whole-program walk.

`KunaCallGraphReader` validates the graph through the shared streaming
document reader. It retains only the facts queries use (126 MB for
Raycast) and checks edges against the complete node set once Kuna
exits. Unrequested bodies are refused before any of their text is
assembled, through new must-be-null row fields; address fields may be
null, as `forwardsTo` is. Malformed graphs are now `AnalysisOutputError`
like the string scan.

`KunaQueryWork.scan` owns the run-and-validate sequence both producers
shared: diagnostics budget, early rejection and retention of
deterministic overflow.

Refs #1957

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(kuna): index call-graph edges as they stream

Review found that the reader kept every parsed edge and built the edge
indexes only after streaming, outside any heap admission, so a large
graph could exhaust the heap instead of returning a memory constraint.

Index each edge when it arrives: duplicate pairs and callee orders are
checked per caller, call edges go straight into the caller/callee
indexes, and no edge array is kept, so the whole working set grows under
the per-row admission. Endpoints and order completeness are checked once
all nodes are known, and the validation-only indexes are released then.
Raycast's graph now peaks at 346 MB instead of 503 MB and retains 93 MB
instead of 126 MB, in the same time.

Also drop imports the shared scan made unused.

commits.subject: fix(pe): ignore zero-extent sections in resource interval ownership (#4463)
commits.body:
fix(pe): ignore zero-extent sections in resource interval ownership (#4463)

Both resource-interval overlap predicates in PeResourceLayout used strict
endpoint inequalities without an extent or point ownership rule, so a
section with VirtualSize=0 and SizeOfRawData=0 inside a resource interval
was rejected as overlapping virtual sections, and the same empty section
inside a header-backed payload was rejected as ambiguous header mapping.
An empty payload at an RVA that starts a positive-extent section below
SizeOfHeaders silently resolved to the header offset even though that
section owns the point.

Normalize intersection once at the owning mapper: a section without
virtual extent owns no byte and never conflicts; an empty resource owns
exactly its start point, so a positive-extent section starting there
conflicts with header-backed ownership and keeps the existing
ambiguous-mapping failure. Positive-extent overlap rejection is
unchanged.

commits.subject: fix(package): parse tar listings without platform line endings (#4315)
commits.body:
fix(package): parse tar listings without platform line endings (#4315)

Windows ships two tar implementations. `C:\Windows\System32\tar.exe` (bsdtar)
terminates every listed member with CRLF, so `verify-package-pack.mjs`
splitting the listing on a bare "\n" left a trailing "\r" on each non-final
member. `verifyPackedBridge` compares member identities exactly, so it reported
`package omitted package/bridge/hopper_bridge.py` although the tarball ships
that member (#4128).

`parseTarListing` normalizes line endings once, at the listing owner, and
preserves every member string beyond its line ending. `verifyPackagePack` is
the only tar listing producer in the package verifiers, so its consumers now
compare bare member names; the prefix checks in the same file keep their
behavior because they never matched a line ending.

Covered by `tests/conformance/package/packedTarListing.test.ts`: CRLF and LF
listings both yield exact bridge identities, the trailing line ending no longer
produces an empty member, member strings keep embedded spaces, and a regression
guard pins the previous parse's failure.

Real Windows 11 evidence (`package/bridge/hopper_bridge.py` in the listing):

| tar                                | listing | split("\n") | parseTarListing |
| ---------------------------------- | ------- | ----------- | --------------- |
| Git for Windows GNU tar            | LF      | true        | true            |
| C:\Windows\System32\tar.exe        | CRLF    | false       | true            |

Fixes #4128

* fix(native): report PE input byte budgets as file-size limits

PeResourcesProvider translated every ArtifactReaderFailure with reason
"limit" into a memory resource constraint, so an image above the
caller's max_file_bytes was reported as a memory problem with memory
remediation advice. The bound that was exceeded is the input file's
byte length, which the caller raises with a flag.

Record the constrained bound on the failure the way ElectronFuseReader
already does, declare it at the reader's two input-byte refusals and at
the parser's metadata and entry budgets, and report that bound instead
of assuming memory. Readers that do not declare a boundary are
unchanged.

* fix(native): keep caller-selected PE budget refusals actionable

Address review findings on the budget classification:

- withCleanup now forwards the constrained bound, so a file that grows past
  its byte limit while its handle also fails to close is still reported as
  a file-size refusal rather than a memory one.
- Both caller-selected bounds carry their own remediation, pointing at
  max_file_bytes and max_entries instead of the file-size fallback's worker
  write-limit advice.
- AnalysisResourceConstraintError can declare that retrying cannot succeed.
  The entry budget is deterministic for the same file and limit, so it no
  longer inherits admission capacity's retryable behaviour.

The projection falls back to the previous resource-kind rule when a caller
does not declare retryability, so other capacity refusals are unchanged.

* fix(native): preserve budget retryability and name the schema ceiling

Address the remaining review findings on the budget classification:

- Failure redaction and the caller-copy path rebuilt resource constraint
  errors without forwarding retryable, so a deterministic capacity refusal
  projected as retryable again and automated callers could loop on it.
  Both constructors now forward the declared boolean.
- Both remediations recommended raising a bound the caller had already
  set to the schema maximum. The maxima are now named constants shared

commits.subject: fix(ghidra): resolve keg-only Homebrew openjdk on macOS (#4556) (#4557)
commits.body:
fix(ghidra): resolve keg-only Homebrew openjdk on macOS (#4556) (#4557)

* fix(ghidra): resolve keg-only Homebrew openjdk on macOS (#4556)

Fixes an issue where the `ghidra-java` check fails when OpenJDK is installed via Homebrew on macOS (where it is keg-only and not added to `PATH` or resolved by `java_home`).

- **Problem:** When `options.javaHome` is undefined, the provider defaulted to a bare `"java"` command, causing valid Homebrew OpenJDK installations to be reported as missing dependencies.
- **Solution:** Replaced the single fallback with an absolute candidate list (`javaCandidates`) that probes standard Homebrew OpenJDK paths (`/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk/...` and `/usr/local/opt/openjdk/...`) before falling back to `"java"`. All candidates are absolute, preserving existing constraints and current behavior.

* fix(ghidra): fix javaHome type narrowing in java candidate list (#4556)

Fixes a TypeScript compilation error (`TS2322` and `TS2345`) in `src/ghidra/GhidraInstallation.ts` where `options.javaHome` was inferred as `string | undefined` inside `path.join()`.

- **Problem:** The ternary operator structure prevented TypeScript from narrowing `options.javaHome` to `string` in the `path.join()` call when `options.javaHome` was defined, causing CI compile checks to fail.
- **Solution:** Refactored the `javaCandidates` assignment using an immediately invoked function expression (IIFE) with an explicit `if (options.javaHome === undefined)` check. This properly narrows `options.javaHome` to `string` in the non-undefined branch while keeping the same logic and Homebrew OpenJDK paths intact.

* fix(ghidra): order homebrew java candidates by host architecture (#4556)

Updates the Homebrew OpenJDK candidate ordering in `src/ghidra/GhidraInstallation.ts` to be architecture-aware, addressing review feedback regarding cross-architecture runs (e.g., x64 under Rosetta on Apple Silicon).

- **Problem:** Previously, `/opt/homebrew` was always checked before `/usr/local`. When running REA as an x64 process under Rosetta on Apple Silicon, this could incorrectly select an ARM64 JDK over an Intel/x64 one, triggering a `nativeDecompilerCheck` failure and missing the valid fallback.
- **Solution:** Dynamically orders `javaCandidates` based on the runtime `architecture`. On `arm64`, `/opt/homebrew` is prioritized; on `x64`, `/usr/local` is prioritized. Bare `"java"` remains first in both cases to preserve standard PATH resolution.

Files above ~5 MB exhaust the worker heap during static analysis (or exceed

The .default(0) gate fix fabricated a measured zero for saved
pre-change evidence, so comparisons would receive a definitive
"no files skipped" fact the producer never established. Use the
codebase's exactOptional idiom instead: legacy reads accept absence
and keep omission (unknown), while the producer still always writes

* fix(kuna): name the setting that owns a timed-out Kuna run

A Kuna run past its deadline surfaced the generic "Analysis took too
long. Try a smaller request" message. The request is already one
function or one whole-program scan, and the same run takes as long
again, so the advice was wrong and REA_KUNA_TIMEOUT_MS or
REA_KUNA_PROJECT_TIMEOUT_MS was never mentioned.

Each Kuna command now carries a KunaDeadline: the configured
milliseconds and the setting that owns them, from KunaConfiguration.
A timeout reports, for example, "kuna decompile did not finish within
REA_KUNA_TIMEOUT_MS (120000 ms)." Its remediation says to raise that
setting and restart REA, and for a single-function decompile that the
session's project export can still answer. AnalysisTimeoutError now
accepts a producer message and remediation, which projection uses and
per-waiter scan errors keep.

commits.body:
fix(setup): read signed 64-bit TOML integers losslessly (#4937)

Codex and Grok client TOML was parsed with smol-toml's default reader,
which rejects any integer beyond JavaScript's safe Number range. Valid
TOML 1.0 Int64 values such as `max_bytes = 9223372036854775807` made
setup, doctor and uninstall treat the whole file as malformed.

The client TOML owner now parses with `integersAsBigInt: "asNeeded"`,
keeping safe integers as numbers and larger ones exact as bigint, and
rejects values outside signed Int64 before any write. All TOML parses in
the document owner (document read, inline string decoding and the
preserving-edit check) use that reader. The inline-table writer emits
bigint values, and setup and doctor accept a positive bigint
`startup_timeout_sec`/`tool_timeout_sec` instead of replacing or
rejecting it.

Fixes #4917

commits.subject: fix(setup): admit only strict JSON for Claude Code configuration (#4944)
commits.body:
fix(setup): admit only strict JSON for Claude Code configuration (#4944)

Claude Code shared the generic `json` client format, which the shared
configuration reader admits through JSONC parsing with comments and
trailing commas enabled. Native Claude Code reads `.claude.json` with a
strict JSON parser (after a UTF-8 BOM), so setup reported `ready`, wrote
a registration into a file the client rejects as corrupt, and doctor
reported it `aligned`.

Give Claude Code its own `claude_code` configuration format and parse it
at the owning boundary with strict JSON.parse after removing a leading
BOM. Setup, doctor, and uninstall all consume that parser, so comment or
trailing-comma documents are now refused as malformed before any backup
or write, while plain and BOM-prefixed JSON still configure. Clients that
natively accept JSONC keep the `json` format and its behavior.

Fixes #4940
